item.title: Evolution-Inspired Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering.
item.abstract: Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution-inspired multi-objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active-learning framework that integrates path-dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi-objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high-value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state-of-the-art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA-binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target-region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two- and three-objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation-derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme-engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus, probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non-native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae, stability-related descriptors identified aggregation-resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi-objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism-derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

item.title: Benchmarking and Experimental Validation of Machine Learning Strategies for Enzyme Engineering.
item.abstract: Enzyme-directed evolution increasingly relies on computational tools to prioritize mutations, yet their practical value is difficult to assess because kinetic data are often aggregated across heterogeneous assay conditions, inflating apparent generalization. Here we introduce EnzyArena, a curated benchmark in which kinetic parameters (kcat, Km, or kcat/Km) are grouped by experimental campaign and measured under matched conditions, thereby minimizing confounders such as pH, temperature, reaction, and batch. Using EnzyArena, we systematically evaluate 20 models spanning four widely used strategies for guiding enzyme evolution: protein-ligand binding affinity prediction, protein stability prediction, zero-shot fitness prediction and enzyme kinetic parameters prediction. Across subsets derived from public databases and 25 literature-derived mutagenesis data sets, most models exhibit weak, fragile, or inconsistent correlation with measured functional outcomes. Kinetic-parameter predictors perform strongly on database-derived subsets but lose their advantage on literature-derived mutagenesis data sets, whereas zero-shot predictors show more consistent generalization. A simple consensus of multiple zero-shot models further improves the precision of identifying beneficial mutants in retrospective analyses. We prospectively validated these findings in a wet-lab campaign (150 mutants) comparing random mutants, UniKP-prioritized mutants, and ESM-1v-prioritized mutants (representing supervised kinetic parameters prediction and zero-shot fitness prediction, respectively), where ESM-1v achieved the highest utility and UniKP underperformed the random baseline. Together, this study establishes realistic baselines for computational mutant prioritization and indicates that zero-shot strategies provide the most consistent, although still modest, performance among the approaches evaluated.

item.title: Refactoring pikromycin synthase for the modular biosynthesis of macrolide antibiotics in E. coli.
item.abstract: While engineering modular polyketide synthases (PKSs) using the recently updated module boundary has yielded libraries of triketide-pentaketides, this strategy has not yet been applied to the combinatorial biosynthesis of macrolactones or macrolide antibiotics. Here we developed a two-plasmid system for the construction and expression of PKSs and used it to obtain a refactored pikromycin PKS in E scherichia coli that produces 49 mg of narbonolide per litre of culture. The replacement, insertion, deletion and mutagenesis of modules enabled access to hexaketide, heptaketide and octaketide derivatives. Supplying enzymes for desosamine biosynthesis and transfer enabled production of narbomycin, pikromycin, YC-17, methymycin and five derivatives thereof. By using native docking domains, knocking out pathways competing with desosamine biosynthesis and supplying the editing thioesterase PikAV, the titre of narbomycin was boosted 58-fold to 37 mg l-1. The second and third modules of the refactored pikromycin synthase were swapped with others to yield three new narbomycin analogues, investigate structure-activity relationships and demonstrate how libraries of macrolide antibiotics can be readily accessed.

item.title: Microbial production of γ-curcumene in metabolically engineered Escherichia coli using a novel γ-curcumene synthase from Parthenium argentatum.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Terpenoids are attractive targets for sustainable biomanufacturing because of their structural diversity and potential applications in fuels and high-value chemicals. Among sesquiterpenes, γ-curcumene is a promising yet underexplored molecule, and its efficient microbial production has not been established. In this study, we identified a previously uncharacterized γ-curcumene synthase PaCS from Parthenium argentatum and evaluated its use for microbial γ-curcumene production in metabolically engineered Escherichia coli.
RESULTS: Sequence analysis revealed that PaCS is phylogenetically distinct from the previously reported γ-curcumene synthase from Pogostemon cablin. When expressed in an E. coli strain carrying a heterologous mevalonate pathway, PaCS predominantly produced γ-curcumene, with only minor formation of (-)-α-bisabolol. Product identity was confirmed by GC-MS and NMR analyses. Biochemical characterization of recombinant PaCS showed maximal activity at 35 °C and pH 8.5, with Mg²⁺ as the preferred divalent metal ion. For microbial production, culture conditions and host background were evaluated, and the evolved strain SBA01 showed the best performance. In fed-batch fermentation, the engineered strain produced up to 1.1 g/L γ-curcumene in terrific broth and 1.03 g/L in modified R medium. In addition, purified γ-curcumene was chemically hydrogenated to bisabolane and dihydro-ar-curcumene, demonstrating its utility as a precursor for fuel-related sesquiterpene hydrocarbons.
CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a microbial production platform for γ-curcumene using a novel γ-curcumene synthase from P. argentatum and metabolically engineered E. coli. The results expand the available terpene synthase toolbox and provide a foundation for the biosynthesis and downstream upgrading of γ-curcumene-derived molecules. These findings support the broader use of synthetic biology and metabolic engineering for the production of non-native sesquiterpenes from renewable carbon sources.

item.title: Liquid biopsy for brain tumors.
item.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Diagnosis and molecular classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors depend largely on neurosurgical sampling, which may be difficult to obtain and is rarely repeated throughout the disease course. This review examines how liquid biopsy may extend molecular assessment of primary and metastatic CNS tumors beyond the initial tissue specimen.
RECENT FINDINGS: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cell-free DNA can identify diagnostically informative alterations in gliomas, CNS lymphoma, and CNS metastases. Serial sampling can reveal evolving tumor clones and resistance-associated alterations absent from archival tissue. Recent advances in error-corrected sequencing, fragment analysis, and methylation classification broaden the molecular information available from blood and CSF. However, diagnostic yield varies with tumor type, anatomical location, sampling compartment, and assay design, and blood-based detection remains challenging in primary brain tumors.
SUMMARY: Liquid biopsy may complement tissue diagnosis, imaging, and conventional CSF studies, particularly when repeat tissue sampling is impractical. Prospective validation is needed to establish standardized workflows, clarify the interpretation of negative results, and determine whether molecular findings improve treatment selection and patient outcomes.

item.title: Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers.
item.abstract: Preoperative discrimination of ovarian cancer from benign masses poses significant challenges, particularly in cases where serum biomarkers yield negative or nonspecific results. This multicenter observational diagnostic modeling study analyzed plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from 743 participants across training, internal test, external test, and two exploratory cohorts using low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Four fragmentomic feature classes-fragment size patterns, nucleosome footprint-related features, copy-number variations, and repeat element patterns-were incorporated into a stacked machine-learning model. Model development and cutoff selection were limited to the training cohort, followed by evaluation in the internal-test and external-test cohorts. The cfDNA model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.930 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.894-0.966) and 0.932 (95% CI, 0.891-0.972) in the internal-test and external-test cohorts, respectively. Incorporation of cfDNA with cancer antigen 125 (CA125) and human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) increased AUCs to 0.964 (95% CI, 0.938-0.990) and 0.964 (95% CI, 0.938-0.991). At cutoffs derived from the training cohort, the combined model maintained sensitivities of 88.4% and 89.2% while enhancing specificity from 77.9% to 88.4% and from 78.9% to 91.5%, respectively. The cfDNA model also effectively detected cancers with CA125 and/or HE4 levels below conventional thresholds, and post hoc analyses demonstrated complementary discrimination when cfDNA was added to the Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm. These findings advocate for prospective evaluation of integrated cfDNA fragmentomics as an adjunct for preoperative risk stratification of ovarian masses.

item.title: Therapeutic Potential of Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Extracellular Vesicles for Tendon Regeneration: Insights into Inflammatory and Angiogenesis Modulation.
item.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) are a promising cell-free therapeutic in preclinical models of tendon healing. However, clinical translation remains to be demonstrated. MSC-EVs modulate two critical and interlinked processes in tendon repair-inflammation and angiogenesis-primarily via delivery of bioactive cargo such as microRNAs and proteins. In inflammation, MSC-EVs promote the transition of macrophages from a pro-inflammatory (M1) to an anti-inflammatory (M2) phenotype, enhancing the resolution of inflammation. In angiogenesis, MSC-EVs facilitate endothelial cell proliferation and migration, promoting early vascularization followed by vascular regression during later healing. Recent advancements in MSC-EVs engineering and delivery systems have improved their therapeutic efficacy, yet further research is essential to elucidate their molecular mechanisms and achieve precise therapeutic outcomes.

item.title: Biochemical profiling of adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell conditioned media: Reproducible protein quantification and growth factor analysis.
item.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cell-conditioned media (MSC-CM) represents a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy in regenerative medicine, leveraging the paracrine effects of stem cells. Standardized biochemical characterization of MSC-CM is crucial for ensuring its reproducibility and therapeutic potential. However, statistical validation of batch-to-batch reproducibility has been rarely reported. Therefore, this study aimed to establish a reproducible protocol for AD-MSC-CM production and quantitatively demonstrate batch-to-batch reproducibility of total protein and key growth factors. Adipose-derived MSCs (AD-MSCs) were isolated from rat adipose tissue, expanded, and used to produce conditioned media (MSC-CM). The MSC-CM was biochemically profiled using the Bradford assay for total protein concentration and specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) for quantifying Transforming Growth Factor-Beta (TGF-β) and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF). Analyses were performed on three independent biological replicates. The MSC-CM showed a significant and consistent increase in total protein concentration compared to control serum-free medium. Quantitative analysis revealed reproducible and stable secretion of key growth factors. The concentrations of both TGF-β and VEGF showed no significant variation across the biological replicates, confirming the high reproducibility of the MSC-CM preparation protocol. This study established a robust method for generating reproducible AD-MSC-CM, characterized by a stable and enriched content of total protein and specific growth factors (TGF-β and VEGF). The findings confirm the reliability of the production process and highlight the hypothesized potential of this well-characterized MSC-CM as a consistent therapeutic agent for applications requiring immunomodulation and angiogenesis, pending direct functional validation.

item.title: Harnessing plant redox networks and bacterial modulation for next-generation abiotic stress resilience in crops.
item.abstract: Abiotic stresses such as drought, salinity, heavy metals, heat, and cold disrupt cellular redox homeostasis, resulting in the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and oxidative damage that negatively affect plant growth and productivity. Under controlled conditions, lower level of ROS act as signaling molecule, whereas, at elevated levels with biotic and abiotic stress factors, causes cellular damage. This review critically examines the molecular mechanisms involved in redox homeostasis in plants, including both enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidant systems. The integrated roles of phytohormone signaling and plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB) in regulating ROS metabolism, boosting antioxidant capacity, and enhancing abiotic stress tolerance are further discussed. Mechanistic insights into plant stress adaptation are provided by evaluating recent advances in transcriptional regulation, epigenetic modification, and redox-associated regulatory networks. Moreover, we review the contributions of multi-omics approaches toward understanding redox regulation and identifying key molecular components involved in stress resilience. Finally, emerging applications of synthetic biology and artificial intelligence are explored as potential tools for engineering redox regulatory networks to accelerate the development of climate-resilient crops. Overall, this review provides an integrated mechanistic framework outlining how redox biology, PGPB interactions, and next-generation engineering strategies can be combined to enhance crop resilience and sustainable agricultural productivity under future environmental shifts.

item.title: Microbiota-dependent biofunctionality of sulfated fucans from Saccharina japonica during intestinal epithelial development in juvenile mice: Limosilactobacillus reuteri L11 as a microbial responder.
item.abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated that sulfated fucans from Saccharina japonica (SJ-FUC) promote intestinal epithelial development in juvenile mice. However, whether this biofunctionality depends on the gut microbiota and which microbial responders contribute to this process remain unclear. Here, we integrated in vitro anaerobic fermentation, metagenomic analysis, antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, bacterial isolation, and juvenile mouse intervention to investigate the microbial basis underlying the intestinal biofunctionality of SJ-FUC. In vitro fecal fermentation showed that SJ-FUC markedly remodeled the gut microbiota derived from both conventional and SJ-FUC-adapted mice and selectively enriched specific bacterial taxa. Limosilactobacillus reuteri exhibited a consistent response to SJ-FUC, with a higher baseline abundance in adapted microbiota and further enrichment after fermentation. In antibiotic-treated mice, microbiota depletion markedly attenuated SJ-FUC-induced intestinal stem cell-associated responses, epithelial proliferation, and secretory lineage differentiation, demonstrating that the intestinal effects of SJ-FUC are largely microbiota-dependent. A strain of L. reuteri, designated L11, was subsequently isolated from the SJ-FUC fecal fermentation system and functionally evaluated in juvenile mice. Both viable L11 and its cell-free supernatant upregulated the intestinal stem cell markers Lgr5, Olfm4, and Ascl2, enhanced Wnt/β-catenin-related gene expression and epithelial proliferation, and promoted secretory lineage differentiation. Overall, these findings establish the gut microbiota as an important contributor to the intestinal biofunctionality of SJ-FUC and identify L. reuteri L11 as a functional microbial responder associated with these effects. This study provides new insight into how an edible-algae-derived sulfated polysaccharide influences juvenile intestinal epithelial development through interactions with the gut microbiota.
